stories.title: Who Decides When an AI System is High-Risk?
stories.teaser: The European Commission has released draft guidelines for classifying artificial intelligence systems as high-risk under the EU AI Act, which aims to regulate AI based on potential harm. However, the Civil Liberties Union for Europe identifies a significant problem, the AI companies themselves largely decide whether their systems qualify as high-risk.

stories.title: AI angst hits New York
stories.teaser: New York politicians are expressing serious concerns about artificial intelligence and pushing for immediate federal action to regulate the technology. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called on Congress to act urgently, while Mayor Zohran Mamdani described recent AI warnings as alarming and said the city would explore options to protect residents.

stories.title: Tech CEOs call for AI regulation but President Trump and Congress are not rushing to act
stories.teaser: Tech leaders including Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Sam Altman of OpenAI, and Elon Musk are calling for greater government oversight of artificial intelligence. However, President Trump and leading Republicans are resisting these efforts, with Trump dismissing regulation calls as a conspiracy.

stories.title: Linden Moves To Prohibit Ai Data Centers Throughout The City - News12
stories.teaser: Representative Gabe Evans introduced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, which passed the House Energy and Commerce Committee unanimously with a 52-0 vote in July. The bill aims to protect communities and existing utility customers from bearing the costs of electrical grid upgrades needed for new data centers.

stories.title: US bishops form new task force over AI concerns, meet with tech leaders
stories.teaser: The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops announced the formation of a new task force on artificial intelligence following a meeting with technology leaders and lawmakers on September 16, 2026.

stories.title: Toledo council members to discuss responsible AI use
stories.teaser: Toledo City Council will hold a meeting on Tuesday, September 15 at 4 p.m. to discuss the responsible use of artificial intelligence. The meeting, led by Council Member Sam Melden who chairs the Economic Development and Innovation Committee, will take place in council chambers at One Government Center.

stories.title: Hmmm: 'Serious Safety Concerns.' Obama Calls for AI Regulations
stories.teaser: Former President Barack Obama called for the U.S. government to establish artificial intelligence safety regulations and standards. In a social media post on September 14, Obama urged Washington leaders to develop concrete laws and regulations addressing serious safety concerns related to AI technology.

stories.title: Microsoft agrees to stronger AI privacy rules for students
stories.teaser: Microsoft has agreed to implement stricter privacy and safety standards for artificial intelligence tools used in schools, following negotiations with the American Federation of Teachers, the country's second-largest teachers union. The legally binding agreement, which takes effect November 1, prohibits Microsoft from using student data to train AI systems, selling data for advertising purposes, or creating AI…

stories.title: Jon Ossoff calls for inspectors at AI research labs amid industry fears
stories.teaser: I don't see an article about Jon Ossoff calling for inspectors at AI research labs in the text provided. The article you've shared is about warnings from AI industry leaders regarding AI safety risks and the potential for artificial intelligence to escape human control.

stories.title: World News: King Charles warns tech leaders of 'existential dangers' from AI
stories.teaser: King Charles hosted leading artificial intelligence figures at his Dumfries House estate in Scotland and warned them about the existential dangers of AI falling into the wrong hands. Attendees included Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis, OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar, Anthropic’s Tino Cuéllar, British AI minister Kanishka Narayan, and an adviser to the pope.

stories.title: Microsoft commits to AI privacy for students. Will others follow?
stories.teaser: Millions of students use AI chatbots daily for schoolwork and personal advice, often without knowing how their data is used. As artificial intelligence becomes embedded in classroom tools, concerns about privacy and data protection have grown among educators, parents and students.

stories.title: The Republican behind the AI ‘kill switch’ battle
stories.teaser: The Times reports that Republican congressman Nathaniel Moran is leading a legislative effort to create an artificial intelligence kill switch or brake. The proposal aims to introduce a safety control while preserving innovation, and Moran is the central figure in what the article describes as a battle over this measure.

incidents.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.teaser: Angela Lipps, 50, a Tennessee mother and grandmother, was arrested at gunpoint by US marshals in July 2025 while babysitting four children. She was falsely charged in Fargo, North Dakota, with four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft.

incidents.title: The man who attacked a Swiss daycare found his victims on ChatGPT
incidents.teaser: A 23 year old Chinese student is on trial in Zurich for attempted murder after stabbing three five year old boys outside a childcare centre in Oerlikon on 1 October 2024. He used a knife with an 8.5 centimetre blade, seriously injuring all three children.

incidents.title: First data breach executed by an artificial intelligence agent autonomously
incidents.teaser: Spain's data protection authority has received the first reported personal data breach carried out by an AI agent. The attacker used a well known language model to search for vulnerabilities, log in successfully, and then autonomously find flaws in an application, modify personal data, and access invoices.

incidents.title: How rogue officers turned a nationwide camera network into a tool for stalking
incidents.teaser: A Kechi police lieutenant, Victor Heiar, was arrested by Wichita police after he allegedly used his department access to Wichita's license plate reader system to track his estranged wife's movements. He has been removed from his job and booked into Sedgwick County Jail on one count of stalking and one count of unlawful acts concerning computers.

incidents.title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.
incidents.teaser: A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant improperly used Flock license plate cameras to look up one plate 41 times and another plate 148 times between January 2022 and December 2025. The lieutenant admitted the searches were not for official law enforcement work.

incidents.title: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.teaser: Parkview High School in Gwinnett County, Georgia received its fourth AI-generated bomb threat of the school year on Monday. School officials placed the school on lockdown out of an abundance of caution, and it later returned to normal operations.
